experiment: Dynamic per-Sim multi-voice English speech synthesis in the Python 3.15 companion

mechanism.voice_selection: Maps Sim gender ('FEMALE' -> Microsoft Zira, 'MALE' -> Microsoft David / Microsoft Mark alternated by voice_actor so two male Sims in a conversation never share the same voice) and scales SSML <prosody pitch> from the Sim's in-game voice_pitch float.
mechanism.synthesis_pipeline: Single-pass SSML <speak> document combining both speaker turns with a 180ms inter-speaker break, rendered to WAV by companion.py before writing reply.json.
mechanism.playback_synchronization: When --speak is enabled, companion.py waits for the game's _ReplyPoller to write {'type': 'displayed', 'event_id': ...} to events.jsonl and plays the pre-rendered WAV asynchronously via winsound.PlaySound so audio starts at the exact moment the visual speech card appears.
mechanism.simlish_suppression_path: Setting 'voiceslevel = 0' in Options.ini (the in-game Voices audio slider) silences Simlish vocalizations on the game's voice mixer channel while preserving sound effects, music, ambient audio, and mouth animations.

limits: Local Windows SAPI voices (Zira, David, Mark) are fast (~0.6-0.8s) and offline, but sound more robotic than neural cloud TTS.
Companion audio plays as 2D stereo via winsound rather than 3D positional game audio.
In-game 'voiceslevel = 0' silences all Simlish across the lot rather than muting only the two conversing Sims.
